A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Articulate-Anything, with matching core methods and traceable retained experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and all appendices support comparison, including v2's added Appendices A.5–A.8.

before.justification: v1 reports original PartNet-Mobility evaluations, modality and iterative-refinement experiments, in-the-wild reconstructions, and simulated robot-learning results.

after.justification: v2 retains original articulation experiments and adds prompt/VLM ablations, mesh-reconstruction measurements, real-robot outcomes and human annotation-time measurements.

M1.justification: The core actor-critic articulation procedure remains intact, but Appendix A.8 adds a substantial alternative to mesh retrieval: Rodin mesh generation followed by video-conditioned Grounded SAM segmentation, multiview projection and transfer of part labels to dense meshes. v1 only proposed upstream mesh reconstruction as future work.

E1.justification: v2 extends the simulation-only robotics application to physical Franka deployment and adds evaluation of human asset-annotation labor. PartNet-Mobility and the existing in-the-wild reconstruction examples remain; additional mesh-quality measurements on those objects do not themselves constitute new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The main URDFormer and Real2Code comparator sets are retained. Section 6 adds human-expert asset annotation using RialTo as a comparator, while Figure 24 qualitatively compares the selected Rodin frontend with Instant Mesh and Stable-Fast-3D. The new matched-modality experiment reuses existing baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds matched-modality comparisons on the baselines' seen classes, actor-only prompt-count and VLM sweeps, and physical robot evaluation with stated physics, scale and pose randomization. New Chamfer evaluations use LiDAR reference meshes and exclude the evaluated object from retrieval candidates. The original articulation thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds sensitivity to prompting examples and VLM choice; Appendix A.5 adds matched-modality controls; Appendix A.6 adds error-distribution and category-based failure analyses. These substantially broaden scrutiny beyond v1's modality and critic-refinement studies. Conversely, v1's RGB-D versus depth-only robot-learning curves are removed.

E5.justification: v2 extends uncertainty reporting to the central benchmark: Figure 5 adds 95% confidence intervals, Table 1 adds confidence intervals for joint-type errors and standard deviations for continuous errors, and Table 3 reports standard deviations. The three-seed robotics statement is retained, but the earlier shaded-standard-deviation learning curves are removed. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: The main 75.0% articulation success result remains unchanged. v2 adds matched-modality results of 40.3% for text and 48.5% for images, prompt/VLM and category results, Chamfer scores, and reported 100% real-robot success with 40.58 minutes of human annotation labor per task. The old RL curves disappear. Table 1 also changes Real2Code Oracle's all-class type error from 0.538 to 0.537 and URDFormer Oracle's OOD origin error from 0.514 to 0.513.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, losses and assumptions in Section 3 and the error definitions in Appendix A.1 remain unchanged, including Equations 1–11. The added reconstruction procedure and experiments introduce no new formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the robotics claim from training manipulation policies in simulation to transferring those policies to a real robotic system. The principal actor-critic, multimodal articulation and 75% benchmark claims, together with the introduction's contribution list, remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking matched-modality advantages to foundation-model common sense and planning, identifies small parts and irregular motion as difficult cases, and suggests camera zoom as a possible remedy. Appendix A.8 also explains why task-conditioned segmentation is needed to avoid under- or over-segmentation. The original retrieval limitation and critic-overconfidence discussion remain.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies placement-API alignment and collision checking, documents the generation/segmentation workflow, and identifies robotic action outputs, randomization and LiDAR reference capture. However, Appendix A.3 removes v1's policy observation descriptions, network architecture, end-effector camera specification and manual reward-design disclosure. Code-access information is substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Rodin, Grounded SAM, RialTo and Instant Mesh for the new generation and robotics experiments. Stable-Fast-3D was already cited in v1. The related-work section and central positioning against URDFormer and Real2Code remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include a rewritten robotics paragraph, local explanatory and cross-reference edits, relocation of baseline details, and new Section 5.4 and Appendices A.5–A.8. The additions do not amount to extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and reorganizes the displays: Table 1 moves to the appendix and gains uncertainty entries; new ablation, annotation-time, distribution and category plots and two reconstruction tables appear. The reconstruction montage gains a generation row, robotics illustrations show transfer to reality, and the old RL learning-curve figure is removed.

improvement.justification: Matched-modality controls, prompt/VLM ablations, and uncertainty and category-level reporting substantially strengthen evidence for the method and address important comparison and robustness gaps in v1. Physical robot demonstrations also extend the earlier simulation-only application. These gains outweigh the loss of RL curves and implementation details, although real-robot trial counts remain unspecified. A new reporting flaw needs correction: Table 2 claims retrieval superiority despite displaying average Chamfer distances of 0.1102 for retrieval versus 0.1085 for Real2Code.
